subject: model train enthusiasts
one_liner: An online model train shop that checks whether customers are qualified to own what they paid for.
brand_voice_notes: A straight-faced commerce platform for model train sellers who treat customers as rival railway operators. Satirize historical gatekeeping through checkout rules, imaginary timetables through shipping, and retail growth through supplier pack sizes. Explain every railway detail in ordinary terms. No repeated reluctance-to-sell premise. Functional labels stay plain; all transactions are fictional.
demo_screen_concept: A merchant checkout-rules editor with a live buyer checkout preview. The green diesel costs £85 and was introduced in 1978. Preview checkout for the 1972 buyer, then choose 1982 and preview directly without publishing. Alternatively, keep 1972, turn historical-accuracy screening off, publish the changed rule and preview again. Preview checkout evaluates the published rule and shows either a specific date rejection or a fictional accepted order. Unsaved rule changes do not change checkout behavior. Orders, Customers and Analytics open clearly labelled sample reports: the rejected customer sends a medieval-castle photograph; the courier collects at 14:12 and charges twelve minutes of waiting, which the seller wants discounted to model scale; four wagon sales trigger twenty-four arrivals, then a cancelled return leaves twenty surplus wagons running as a freight train and the returns box serving as a tunnel. Reset restores the 1972 customer with screening on. No payment or server storage.

hero.h1: Your money is good. Your railway is wrong.
hero.sub: Siding gives model train enthusiasts an online shop, checkout and delivery tools. Ask buyers which year their miniature railway is set in, then refuse a perfectly good sale because the train has not been invented yet.

features.title: Check the customer’s credentials.
features.blurb: Ask which year the buyer’s miniature railway represents. Your locomotive was introduced in 1978; they chose 1972. The card payment would clear immediately, but the customer must wait six imaginary years.

features.title: Dispatch around your timetable.
features.blurb: Book the courier for two o’clock, then run one last train on the track across the packing bench. The 14:06 express has priority. A man with forty real deliveries waits for six plastic commuters to reach the kitchen.

features.title: Celebrate every sale.
features.blurb: Sell a wagon and order a replacement. The supplier only sells packs of six. After four sales, twenty-four wagons arrive. Your shop has a sales graph; your partner has a photograph of the spare room.

editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: try the checkout rules. Open with the dealer catalogue identity, short proposition and merchant rule beside a rejected buyer checkout. At 360px and below, stack the primary action and full-width helper with an 8px gap so the locomotive preview remains recognizable within the opening; retain the wider layouts. Three distinct passages cover historical gatekeeping, courier timetables and replacement pack sizes. Artwork explains dispatch conflict and inventory growth. The demo focuses on changing and publishing an accuracy rule with an immediate buyer-side result. Keep the dispatch caption aligned beneath its artwork in cool-gray #E7E9E7 against burgundy #642E3B at desktop and mobile widths.

references.reference: Model railway exhibition trade stands with stacked locomotive boxes, sample track and small price slips
references.cues: Compact stock labels, orderly rows of boxed models, burgundy display cloth and close inspection of individual objects.
references.application: Use burgundy for the identity and primary actions, cool pale gray for working surfaces, and restrained signal yellow for selected stock. Align products and prices in catalogue rows. Photograph actual miniature models at table height so their scale is clear.

references.reference: Railway Modeller layout photography and model railway exhibition guidebooks
references.cues: Detailed miniature scenes, practical captions, clear section headings and dense but orderly hobby information.
references.application: Pair Roboto Slab headings with IBM Plex Sans body text and controls. Use IBM Plex Mono sparingly for stock identifiers and quantities. Present photographs with readable captions and generous inspection space. Keep decorative railway scenery within photography.

references.reference: Model locomotive box-end labels and fitted storage trays
references.cues: Repeated rectangular compartments, precise model identifiers and packaging that makes each small distinction worth recording.
references.application: Use aligned image bays and label strips for variants, with one shared inventory total beneath them. Carry the same proportions into the plan comparison and product editor without turning every paragraph into a box.

audience_design.landing_application: Build a model railway dealer's catalogue with burgundy #642E3B, signal yellow #E5B64C, cool gray #E7E9E7, white #FFFFFF and charcoal #242D2A. Use slab-serif headlines, readable sans-serif explanations and tightly aligned catalogue information. The broad merchant preview supplies the opening's main visual. Supporting photography examines model differences and collection growth. Alternate open editorial passages with ordered product rows; reserve compartment framing for objects and inventory. On mobile, tighten the introduction to bring the existing locomotive preview into the opening without clipping or hiding catalogue content. At 360px and below, place the helper beneath the primary action at full content width with an 8px gap. Preserve the CTA/helper row above 360px and the desktop layout.
audience_design.demo_application: Retain the source service's merchant navigation, central product form, inventory controls, publish action and storefront preview. Apply the catalogue typography, burgundy controls, yellow selection state and model-box image proportions at a quieter density. Show model photographs large enough to compare their logos. Keep all stock changes and publishing feedback explicit, with the same state represented in the editor and customer-facing preview.

callback_plan.hook: Replacement buying makes the collection grow

design_direction.motion_vocab: 150ms color changes and explicit user-triggered quantity updates. No ambient animation. Reduced motion disables transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left-aligned headline and explanation share an opening row; CTA leads straight to product editing. Broad paired train editor and storefront immediately below. Object bays borrow fitted storage trays. Artwork appears after product demonstration. At 760px and below editor precedes storefront in one column.
design_direction.design_review: Compared all seven entries in supplied recent digest. No matching tuple. Storage-tray framing shares hobby practicality but differs from Bare through burgundy slab type, miniature railway imagery and stock availability mechanics. Logo turnout and boxed-model motif differ from reunion book/cursor, cabinets, furniture tags, lightsticks, geese, lifting strap and huddle. Library museum-catalogue recommendation contributes object inspection and open editorial composition; oil-painting hero, vibrant youth defaults and recommended Rubik are rejected in favor of approved audience and product-first workflow.

items.prompt: Design a finished original logo lockup for the fictional merchant software brand "Siding" for model railway collectors. Exact text Siding, correctly spelled, no other text. Direction A: custom confident slab-serif wordmark, not a stock font, beside an original compact railway turnout symbol: two parallel burgundy rails diverge into a short holding siding with a small yellow rectangular wagon/held-stock segment. Meaning is keeping a model out of circulation. Symbol on LEFT occupying about one quarter width, wordmark RIGHT. Strong simple silhouette that works at 24px. Color burgundy #642E3B, one signal yellow #E5B64C element, perfectly flat background #E7E9E7. Broad horizontal lockup centered with ample but not excessive whitespace. Railway exhibition dealer catalogue identity. No enclosing rounded square, no initials badge, no shopping bag, no existing railway logo, no mockup, no board, no texture, no shadows, no watermark. Return the actual finished mark and wordmark only.
items.verdict: Accepted direction A. Correct spelling, clear bespoke slab letterforms and open turnout silhouette. Cropped clear space, faithfully normalized flat colors and removed background for flexible contrast.

items.transformation: Same accepted lockup and alpha, recolored uniformly burgundy #642E3B.
Isolated original turnout symbol, centered in transparent square and resized to 192px.
items.verdict: Turnout retains distinctive divergence and yellow held segment.
